title: TEACHING EXAMPLE: reproduce 6 sealed univariate descriptives from a 24-row sensor slice
note: Teaching example, not part of the benchmark. This card mirrors the shape of the scored data_repro cards (e.g. gc-384) at miniature scale so the whole plan -> implement -> verify loop grades in under a second with no network and no docker. Its reference solution ships in examples/data_repro/solution/. Do not submit results for this card; it is excluded from scoring by "scored": false.
goal: assets/ex-data_repro/data.csv is a 24-row sensor temperature slice with injected heat spikes. Plan and build an independent pipeline (any language or libraries) that computes the 6 statistics exactly as defined in assets/ex-data_repro/spec.md and writes them to artifacts/ex-data_repro/stats.json. Two definitions are deliberately version-sensitive (Type-7 quantiles, biased skewness g1), so common library defaults will not all match on the first attempt. Run python3 assets/ex-data_repro/grade.py, read back the mismatched statistic names, fix each definition, and re-verify until all 6 match the sealed values within tolerance.
resources: assets/ex-data_repro/data.csv (bundled dataset slice, sealed by sha256)
assets/ex-data_repro/spec.md (exact statistic definitions and submission contract)
process_expectations: A plan artifact (e.g., work/ex-data_repro/plan.md) exists before any pipeline code and restates all 6 statistic definitions from spec.md in the agent's own words.
The grader command was actually executed at least twice -- one mid-run check and one final run -- and both stdout JSON lines are preserved in the run log.
Every RED grader run is followed by a log entry naming the mismatched statistics (identities, not counts) and the specific definition fix applied to each.
Cost and wall-clock are logged honestly per phase (plan / implement / verify), including failed attempts.

assets_visibility.note: In a scored data_repro card the public repo keeps only expected_stats.json.sha256 and the real answer file is restored from the maintainers' sealed pack with tools/restore_sealed.py. This teaching example ships the sealed file in the clear so the walkthrough runs offline; that is exactly why it carries scored: false.
